name: BESS
full_name: Balloon-borne Experiment with a Superconducting Spectrometer
summary: Historical Japanese–US balloon superconducting-magnetic-spectrometer series constraining dark-matter models through antiproton, antideuteron and antinucleus searches.
detection_principle: A superconducting magnetic spectrometer measures rigidity; time of flight and particle identification determine charge, speed and mass to search for rare antinuclei.

status.evidence: The 2024 result uses the 2007–2008 BESS-Polar II flight, not new data taken in 2024.

results.summary: BESS-Polar II found no antideuteron candidates and improved flux upper limits.

science_scope: Tests dark-matter models through astrophysical radiation, cosmic rays or neutrinos. Astrophysical backgrounds and propagation models affect interpretation; an anomaly alone does not establish dark matter.
